01 / The interface

From device utility
to daily companion.

The earlier UI is direct and functional. The redesign gives the same core controls a warmer home, adds room for base positioning and insight, and makes the main destinations easier to recognize.

Tonight / temperature

Redesigned + expanded

01A clearer starting point

The original screen devotes most of its height to the temperature ring. Tonight introduces a headline, connection state and the selected side before grouping temperature, base position and comfort settings into separate cards.

02Preview, then apply

The large target value remains easy to find. A linear slider, current-temperature label and explicit Set temperature action distinguish the draft from the running setting. That extra tap is intentional; the old dial is faster for a quick adjustment.

03The whole bed has its own controls

The new Ultra card adds a bed illustration, Flat/Sleep/Relax/Read presets, separate head and feet angles, reported positions, Move bed and Stop. The illustration previews a request; it is not proof that the hardware moved.

04More capability, more scrolling

Adaptive comfort and the last-night summary make Tonight useful beyond the thermostat. On a phone this is a longer screen. Alarm and priming banners remain visible when relevant; a more compact nighttime view is a sensible future refinement.

Metrics → Sleep

New overview; detail retained

01Lead with understandable patterns

The old metrics page emphasizes heart rate, HRV, breathing and a dense trace. The new overview leads with bed presence, bedtime variation, heart rate and recorded-night count, followed by a date-based chart.

02Make missing data visible

The 7/30/90-day selector establishes the comparison window. Recorded nights are counted explicitly. Missing values stay unknown, and Pod presence is described as presence rather than a sleep-duration or sleep-quality claim.

03Give personal context a place

The morning check-in adds restfulness, temperature comfort and optional habit notes. Numerical habit associations can inform coaching; the notes themselves stay on the Pod under the current sharing contract.

04Keep access to the underlying records

Raw vitals and recorded episodes remain accessible on web. HRV and breathing estimates are marked experimental. Native detail browsing and identical journal controls still need work.

Schedules → Routines

Partial visual refresh

01A consistent shell

Routines inherits the cream canvas, common side selector, white cards and labeled navigation. Day selection, on/off times, starting temperature, adjustments and vibration alarm remain part of the workflow.

02Existing behavior stays recognizable

The step chart and expandable editors preserve the familiar scheduling model, including copying a configuration to other days. This makes the transition less disruptive for existing users.

03The redesign is not finished here

The blue/red chart, older slider styling and field arrangement remain visible. It would be inaccurate to call this screen a complete new editor or claim identical native and web layouts.

04The next design decision

Use one readable overnight timeline on both platforms, a common day picker, a change preview and clearer next-alarm behavior. This is a prerequisite for the proposed natural-language routine composer.

Settings → Connections + setup

Reorganized entry point

01Start with how you connect

The archived settings view begins with timezone, units, reboot, LEDs and Pod information. The new entry screen begins with the Pod/gateway address, connection token and appearance selection.

02Explain each Apple surface

Apple Home and Health/Shortcuts receive their own contextual cards. Web points to the native iPhone workflow for Health permissions; it does not pretend a browser can directly access HealthKit.

03Keep advanced controls reachable

Device settings, system health and logs remain linked below the primary setup cards. Operational detail remains available without dominating the first view.

04Guided setup is still needed

These cards are not evidence of a paired Home bridge, working cloud deployment or granted Health permissions. A shared setup checklist with real connection tests would improve first-run clarity; native permission screens will necessarily remain platform-specific.

Scroll inside each capture or open it at full size. The archive includes phone status bars; new web captures are browser content. Long web captures retain the fixed navigation at its original viewport position. Those capture differences are not product defects or a controlled usability test.

02 / The design language

A blend of your
three references.

The direction combines warm surfaces, restrained orange, quiet borders and compact workspace navigation, informed by replit-travel-1, Grid-by-Replit and grep-v2.

  1. One recognizable homeThe desktop sidebar keeps the same destination names as the phone’s bottom navigation.
  2. Color earns its placeOrange is reserved for actions and selected controls. Status colors have their own roles.
  3. Information in layersHeadlines and metrics come first; raw records and advanced settings remain reachable.
  4. Shared rules, native renderingBoth platforms use system fonts and generated tokens. iOS remains a SwiftUI app.

03 / Native iPhone

The same direction.
A real native app.

These are simulator captures of SwiftUI, cropped from the existing simulator mirror. They show shared styling, simulated controls and text scaling. They do not establish complete visual parity or working signed-device integrations.

Completed follow-up · f5e2b51

One alarm change. The same flow on both platforms.

The original design captures above predate this addition. These later captures show the implemented change, skip and restore flow in the web demo and isolated iPhone simulator.

Recorded validation: 41 server tests, 18 native tests and five gateway tests passed for this milestone, plus browser/simulator interactions. No live vibration or signed-device Siri run was performed. Changing an alarm does not move the routine’s power-off time.

What still separates web and iOS

The shared design system is in place. The remaining product differences are concrete:

  • Native alarm picker/sheet chrome and notification presentation; the change, skip and restore actions now match.
  • Recorded-episode and raw-vitals browsing.
  • Matching journal and Coach form controls.
  • A common Routines editor and copy-days flow.
  • Consistent connection and advanced-settings layouts.
  • Platform-specific Health and Home permission flows.

Routines work is in progress; these remaining differences still need validation. OS chrome and accessibility reflow should remain native even when the common app screens match.

04 / New capabilities

More than a
change of palette.

Some screens have no old counterpart. Their current value is a working local foundation, with clear boundaries around what still needs hardware or account validation.

Coaching with a visible sharing choice

Local observations are available without a model. Optional provider adapters can explain a numerical summary. HealthKit records are not automatically included, and the model has no device-control tools.

Comfort that learns within limits

Morning check-ins can inform a bounded temperature offset. Off, Preview and enabled modes keep the behavior understandable; presence, alarms, away mode and manual interaction constrain it. This is feedback-based control, not a reproduced proprietary sleep-stage Autopilot.

Native Health, Home and Shortcuts foundations

The iPhone app provides personal-side Health workflows and typed native actions. A local Home bridge can expose supported bed controls. Source builds and simulated checks exist; real permissions, pairing, Siri and overnight behavior remain to be qualified.

05 / The next twelve

Useful intelligence.
Built on evidence.

These are proposals, not features already shipped. Priority reflects user value and dependencies; effort is a relative engineering estimate, not a delivery promise. Each proposal builds on what is already in the repository.

Start with trust, then add convenience.

My first release would combine data-quality explanations (#9), the AI quality/cost foundation (#3), and an evidence-linked morning brief (#1). Expand the Health timeline (#2) after signed-device checks. Physical automation comes after real Pod and Home qualification.

01 / Daily insightFirst · Medium

A morning brief with receipts

Open the app to one useful observation, the nights behind it, and one optional next step.

“Your bedtime was more consistent on 5 recorded nights. See the dates.”

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
Coach currently answers an explicit request. Add a saved daily brief, delivery preference, and an evidence drawer that links each statement to source dates and computed metrics.
How AI fits
Calculate facts locally, then ask the chosen language model to explain an allowlisted fact set in a typed response. Start with GPT-6.1 Sol and compare Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash. Render a deterministic brief if no cloud sharing is enabled.
Needs first
A versioned evidence record, wake-date/timezone handling, freshness checks and opt-in delivery. Pod presence must remain distinct from measured sleep.
Done when
Every numerical statement resolves to a stored calculation; missing or sparse nights cause abstention; the same evidence opens on web and iOS. No model may invent a score or a sleep stage.
OpenAI · GPT-6.1 Sol ↗OpenAI · Structured Outputs ↗Google Research · Anatomy of a personal health agent ↗
02 / Connected contextFirst · Large

One timeline for Apple Health and your bed

See Watch sleep, Pod presence, temperature changes and morning feedback on one clearly sourced timeline.

Tap a restless interval to see what was recorded, by which device, and what is missing.

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
The native app already has personal-side Health sync and local comparison. Extend this to an aligned timeline with source filters and explicit overlap resolution; add an opt-in derived-summary path for web parity.
How AI fits
Keep alignment and statistics deterministic. Offer an optional explanation of selected intervals, using only the aggregates the user chooses to share. Use wearable-model research as a future evaluation direction, not as a replacement for source provenance.
Needs first
Signed-device HealthKit validation, per-type consent, a stable personal-side binding, timestamp normalization and clear handling of multiple sleep sources. Web cannot query HealthKit directly.
Done when
Duplicate sources never double-count time. Users can inspect origin, revoke sharing and remove synchronized summaries. A missing Health sample never becomes a fabricated zero or an inferred stage.
Apple · HealthKit ↗Google Research · SensorFM ↗
03 / FoundationFirst · Medium

A quality and cost center for AI

Choose a provider with visible evidence, a monthly budget and an understandable privacy setting.

“Local only” or “Cloud summaries · chosen provider · usage this month.”

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
Provider adapters and explicit sharing already exist. Add a repeatable evaluation set, model/version history, usage accounting, a hard request budget and a user-visible comparison of tested results.
How AI fits
Benchmark Sol, Sonnet and Flash on identical de-identified or synthetic cases. Include Gemini 4 Argon as a deeper-reasoning challenger. Test factual grounding, numbers, missing data, misleading notes, response time and total billed tokens. A second model may flag issues but cannot define the ground truth. For the native coach, use Apple’s new Evaluations framework with the same evidence fixtures and measured criteria.
Needs first
Provider keys for live evaluation, expected answers from deterministic calculations, per-provider retention settings and a budget ledger. Cloud data never silently switches to another vendor.
Done when
All critical fixtures pass with zero fabricated measurements or device commands. The budget blocks further paid calls at its configured ceiling. Publish measured quality/cost results before changing the default.
OpenAI · GPT-6.1 Sol ↗Anthropic · Current model catalog ↗Google · Gemini model catalog ↗Google · What’s new in Gemini 4 Argon ↗Apple · Meet the Evaluations framework, WWDC26 ↗
04 / PrivacyNext · Large

A private coach that works offline

Ask about your recent pattern on your iPhone without sending your night to a cloud provider.

“What changed this week?” answered from local, cited facts even without Wi-Fi.

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
The server supports a separately installed Ollama model. Add an on-device iOS coach and an editable, deletable memory of user-approved preferences. Keep the same brief and evidence layout on the web.
How AI fits
Use Apple Foundation Models where available, with guided output and a small local evidence index. Use deterministic summaries on unsupported iPhones; a capable Mac/PC can serve the optional local web model. Do not put a large language model on the Pod.
Needs first
OS/device availability checks, a local evaluation suite, explicit memory controls and shared output contracts. Cloud escalation requires a user choice.
Done when
Airplane-mode tests produce grounded answers on eligible devices; older supported iOS versions render useful fallback summaries. Deleting a memory removes it from subsequent prompts.
Apple · Foundation Models framework ↗Apple · What’s new in Foundation Models, WWDC26 ↗
05 / LearningNext · Large

Personal experiments, one change at a time

Turn “I think cooler helps” into a small, optional experiment with a clear result and honest uncertainty.

Compare your usual setting with a user-selected 1°F change over balanced nights, then review comfort ratings.

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
The journal already shows habit associations and adaptive comfort learns a bounded offset. Add a guided experiment planner, baseline period, adherence tracking and a review screen.
How AI fits
Let the model explain a predefined protocol. Assign conditions and calculate differences locally, accounting for missed nights and obvious confounders. Use perceived comfort as the primary outcome until other measures are validated.
Needs first
Enough baseline observations, repeat check-ins, user-chosen boundaries, a pause control and qualification of any scheduled temperature changes on real hardware.
Done when
Only one variable changes per protocol; incomplete data yields an inconclusive result; every change remains reversible. Observational habit patterns are never presented as proof of causation.
Google Research · Anatomy of a personal health agent ↗OpenAI · Structured Outputs ↗
06 / ComfortLater · Large

Predictive comfort before bedtime

Have the bed approach your chosen temperature at bedtime using its measured heating and cooling behavior.

“Start preparation at 9:12 to target 9:30” with a visible forecast and uncertainty range.

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
Current adaptive comfort adjusts from morning feedback with strict limits. Add a thermal-response forecast, optional room context and a shadow mode that records predictions without controlling the bed.
How AI fits
Start with a simple per-side thermal model. Evaluate TimesFM 2.5 as an offline challenger on a capable local host. A deterministic controller applies validated limits; the LLM only explains the plan. TimesFM 3 self-hosted weights are not a production option under their current license.
Needs first
Real target/actual temperature history, room-temperature data if available, power/presence context and overnight hardware qualification. Performance must be evaluated on held-out nights.
Done when
Forecast error improves on a simple baseline before activation. Shadow mode, stale-data rejection, manual override, away/alarm guards and rollback all pass physical-device tests.

07 / Low-friction inputNext · Medium

A 20-second spoken morning check-in

Hold a button, say how the night felt, and review a short check-in before saving it.

“Too warm around three; felt okay this morning” becomes editable comfort and restfulness fields.

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
Replace repetitive form entry with an optional voice path while keeping the existing accessible text form.
How AI fits
Try local dictation first. Offer Gemini 3.8 Live for an explicitly selected conversational mode. Convert speech into typed fields, preserve uncertainty, and require the user to confirm the result.
Needs first
Microphone permission, a visible recording indicator, explicit cloud-audio choice and a clear retention setting. Avoid capturing a sleeping partner with always-on listening.
Done when
Ambiguous times or negations require correction instead of silent guesses. Cancel discards unsaved audio/transcript data; saving never triggers a device action.

Describe a routine; review the exact changes

Build a schedule in natural language and inspect every affected day, side and setting before applying it.

“On weekdays, warm my side at 9:30 and turn it off at 7” becomes a visible schedule diff.

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
The app already edits schedules and exposes native actions. Add a common web/iOS routine composer that produces the same validated plan, plus a Shortcut entry point for drafting it.
How AI fits
Constrain the model to a schedule schema. Resolve dates and daylight-saving transitions in application code. Apply only a user-confirmed plan through existing authenticated services; keep model tools read-only.
Needs first
Finish and validate the common Routines editor; that work is currently in progress. One-time alarm change/skip/restore is already implemented and locally validated in f5e2b51. Preserve unknown schedule fields, provide rollback, and resolve ambiguous weekdays, sides and overnight intervals.
Done when
A DST/timezone fixture suite passes. The preview shows all edits and any rejected request. No base movement, schedule write or temperature command occurs during generation.

09 / Trustworthy analyticsFirst · Medium

Explain changes and detect bad data

Distinguish a real shift in your routine from a missing night, an offline sensor or a changed data source.

“This week has only two recorded nights, so a trend would be misleading.”

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
Current analytics preserve unknown values. Add completeness indicators, signal-quality history, comparisons that control for recorded-night count, and a “Why did this change?” drawer.
How AI fits
Use deterministic checks and robust personal baselines for quality signals. Give the model read-only, typed access to calculations and source metadata, so explanations point to exact evidence rather than making arithmetic up.
Needs first
Ingestion timestamps, device/source identifiers, missingness flags and a baseline policy. General wearable foundation models require separate Pod-specific evaluation before any use.
Done when
Injected outages, clock shifts and duplicate records are identified without becoming health alerts. No diagnosis, apnea detector, readiness score or sleep stage is inferred from presence alone.

Position profiles that remember comfort

Save your preferred reading or resting position and compare how comfortable it felt over time.

Read the proposal, dependencies & acceptance
What changes
Head/feet sliders, presets and a reported-position view already exist. Add user-named profiles, feedback history and optional recommendations based on the positions the user has actually tried.
How AI fits
Use a small transparent ranking model for preference learning; use an LLM only to explain the evidence. Recommendations are drafts. Whole-bed movement remains a deliberate physical action.

What changes

Apple’s 2026 framework additions broaden private, native AI workflows. Current cloud catalogs offer stronger reasoning alongside specialist voice models. Those capabilities make the proposed input and explanation features practical to evaluate.

01 / Observe

Keep source, side, timestamps and missingness with every record.

02 / Calculate

Compute metrics, comparisons and bounds in testable application code.

03 / Explain

Give the chosen model a minimal evidence bundle and validate its response.

04 / Review & act

Show a plan. Existing authenticated controllers execute only approved, valid actions.

Cost illustration: at Sol’s listed standard rate of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, 4,000 input + 800 total billed output tokens costs $0.016, or $0.48 for 30 such calls. This excludes extra reasoning beyond that output allowance, retries, tools, voice, hosting and hardware. It is arithmetic, not a measured bill or a subscription-equivalence claim. Primary sources & why they matter

  1. OpenAI · GPT-6.1 Sol ↗

    Current model capabilities and standard token pricing. Candidate for concise cloud coaching; no sleep-specific evaluation has been run.

  2. OpenAI · Structured Outputs ↗

    Schema-constrained output can shape a routine or brief. Application validation must still check every value and action.

  3. Anthropic · Current model catalog ↗

    Sonnet 5.5 is a balanced challenger; the catalog also includes Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1. Bigger models are optional evaluation candidates, not automatic upgrades.

  4. Google · Gemini model catalog ↗

    Lists Gemini 4 Argon, 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Live as stable. Different models serve reasoning, responsive summaries and spoken interaction.

  5. Google · What’s new in Gemini 4 Argon ↗

    Current flagship supports tunable reasoning. Introductory pricing ends 30 November 2026; evaluate quality and full reasoning-token cost before adopting.

  6. Google · Live API ↗

    Realtime audio makes an optional spoken check-in feasible. It adds microphone, connection and audio-retention decisions.

  7. Apple · Foundation Models framework ↗

    Native Swift APIs now cover on-device models, guided generation, image understanding and other model providers. Feature availability must be checked at runtime.

  8. Apple · What’s new in Foundation Models, WWDC26 ↗

    2026 additions include vision, context management, semantic search and broader model integration. Our iOS 18 minimum requires a fallback path.

  9. Google Research · SensorFM ↗

    9 July 2026 research on general representations for wearable signals. A research direction, not a validated drop-in model for Pod sleep stages.

  10. Google Research · TimesFM releases and weight licenses ↗

    August–September 2026 brought TimesFM 3 multivariate forecasting and cloud rollout. Self-hosted 3.0 weights are non-commercial/non-production; weights through 2.5 remain Apache-2.0. Authorized cloud production use has separate terms.

  11. Google Research · Anatomy of a personal health agent ↗

    30 September 2025 foundational research separates data analysis, domain context and coaching. Useful architecture guidance; not a clinical endorsement of this app.

  12. Apple · HealthKit ↗

    Native, authorized access to personal health records. Data origin and the user’s selected bed side remain essential.

  13. Apple · Apple Home ↗

    Platform context for user-selected Home accessories and scenes. A LAN bridge and real pairing still need qualification.

  14. Apple · App Intents ↗

    Typed actions for Shortcuts and system surfaces. Discovery in a build is distinct from execution on a signed phone.

  15. Apple · Meet the Evaluations framework, WWDC26 ↗

    The new framework integrates datasets, quantitative metrics and model-judged criteria with Swift Testing. Use it to qualify the native coach across model and prompt changes; ground numerical truth in application calculations.

07 / Evidence & remaining work

A review you
can trace.

This document preserves the distinction between code, a rendered demo, a deployed app and a physically verified bed. The screenshot and source inventory is also recorded alongside this file in the repository.

How the comparison was made

Before: repository archives docs/on.PNG, metrics.PNG, schedules.PNG and settings.PNG. Their original capture dates and exact build revisions are not recorded.

Now: web demo captures taken on 14 October 2026 from the design milestone e05cd99; native images use the existing parity-validation captures. The current app sources were checked against docs/DESIGN_PARITY.md, docs/VALIDATION.md and design/tokens.json.

All new app images show simulated data. Different values, selected dates and banners are not evidence of a health improvement. Native captures are center crops of simulator-mirror images; no UI has been redrawn. The alarm follow-up in the iOS section adds captures from the completed milestone f5e2b51. Uncommitted Routines work is in progress and is not represented as a completed or validated feature.

What should happen before release

Complete common screens: finish Routines, journal, raw-data and Settings parity, then compare both platforms with the same data and state.

Qualify the owner’s setup: verify stock-Pod access and recovery, base telemetry and Stop, actual temperature control and overnight behavior. No installation or bed movement was performed for this document.

Prove the integrations: signed iPhone Health/Shortcuts tests, actual Home pairing, and an authenticated Replit deployment with reconnect and offline checks. None follows from a simulator screenshot.

Evaluate AI: run the grounded test set with the selected account/model, then enable a bounded pilot. This research did not send personal records to providers.
